topic: 5 prompts that make any AI stop writing like an AI
angle: Everyone can smell AI writing now — the fix is five specific constraints, not a better model
hook: 5 prompts that make any AI stop writing like a robot
caption:
Everyone can smell AI writing now. The tell isn't the model — it's the five defaults every model ships with: connector words, uniform sentence length, no reader in mind, a summary paragraph nobody asked for, and hedging on every claim.

These five constraints fix all of it. They work in Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini — paste them as-is, or stack them into one system prompt and never think about it again.

Can you spot AI writing instantly — yes or no? 👇

#aitools #chatgpt #claudeai #writingtips #promptengineering #contentcreation #aiwriting #freelancing

slides.text: 5 prompts that make any AI stop writing like a robot

slides.title: Ban the connectors
slides.body: Paste this: "Rewrite without these words — delve, moreover, furthermore, in conclusion, it's worth noting, landscape, tapestry. No em-dashes." Those seven words carry most of the AI smell. Strip them and the text reads human before you change anything else.

slides.title: Force sentence variance
slides.body: Every model writes in one rhythm: 15 to 20 words, every line. Real writing does not. Tell it: "Vary sentence length. At least one sentence under five words, one over twenty-five." This single constraint does the most work of the five.

slides.title: Give it one reader
slides.body: "Write this for a 28-year-old freelancer who has already tried two AI tools and thinks they are overhyped." Generic audience produces generic prose. One named skeptical reader forces specifics, objections, and a real voice into the draft.

slides.title: Kill the wrap-up
slides.body: AI ends everything with a summary paragraph restating what you just read. Tell it: "End on your last real point. No conclusion, no summary, no 'in short'." You will cut roughly fifteen percent of every draft and lose nothing.

slides.title: Make it commit
slides.body: "Take a position. Remove every hedge — might, could, arguably, some would say, it depends." Hedging is why AI writing feels weightless. A model that commits to a claim sounds like a person who has actually done the thing.

slides.text: Save this before your next draft. Which one are you missing?
